text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Chairman of Bosnia's presidency, Alija Izetbegovic, welcomes appointment of new High Representative to Bosnia, Carlos Westendorp, saying that the job carries tremendous responsibility and Bosnians have high expecations.

- Visit of U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright to Bosnia represented fresh American diplomatic initiative which is being pursued with much more energy and enthusiasm than before, says Mirza Hajric, aide to Izetbegovic.
- Two ruling parties in the divided town of Mostar signed an agreement on establishing six municipalities as defined by the 1995 Dayton peace agreement.
- Austrian government donated 450,000 German marks for the reconstuction of the national library in Sarajevo which was heavily destroyed during the war.
- Bosnian parliament must adopt economic reform laws to clear the way for international donors conference for reconstruction aid due to be held on June 24.
- Municipal elections in September will not be postponed, says David Foley, spokesman for the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE).

- Draft customs law before the parliament provides exemptions for diplomats, international organisations, refugees and displaced persons, says Nikola Grabovac, deputy minister of foreign trade. By arriving at an average of custom rates in Serb and Moslem-Croat entities, the bill would reduce custom fees for computers, wine, meat and milk. -- Sarajevo newsroom +387-71-663-864
